resources.string: Sign in and choose which repositories the agent may read or change
Device-code sign-in: a short code appears here, you approve it on github.com. No token to paste.
Signed in · the agent acts as this account
The token is stored sealed with a key held by the Android Keystore and never shown. Signing out deletes it; the repository permissions below are kept.
After signing in, pick which repositories the agent can reach. Nothing is reachable until you allow it: a repository outside this list does not exist for the GitHub tools.
Open github.com/login/device in a browser, enter this code, and approve the sign-in. This dialog closes by itself once GitHub confirms.
\"All repositories\" makes every repository readable; writing still has to be allowed per repository. \"Only the ones I allow\" hides everything that is not listed below.
Tap \"Read\" or \"Write\" to allow a repository. Use the search to find one that is not listed yet. Write means: commit on new branches and open pull requests, never directly to main.
Everything the account can reach is readable. Tap \"Write\" to also allow commits and pull requests on that repository.
No repository matches. Refresh, or check that the account can see it.
Every repository goes back to read-only. Branches and pull requests already created stay.
